message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a block-breaking game (Breakout/Arkanoid). Let me build a rich, polished single-file HTML game with canvas. Design direction: Arcade cabinet aesthetic. The most characteristic thing for a breakout game is the playfield itself, so I'll open with the game immediately — the canvas front and center, with an arcade cabinet frame, CRT scanlines, side panels with score/lives/level, a marquee at top. Palette: I want a real arcade cabinet feel, so a deep midnight-teal base rather than a flat near-black with a single glowing accent — that would look generic and wouldn't feel like a lit cabinet. Let's do a warm arcade palette: deep navy/ink background with amber, coral, cyan, lime accents — multiple hues, like a lit cabinet. Blocks colored in a spectrum of arcade colors. Background: layered — subtle grid, drifting gradient glow, parallax starfield inside the playfield, plus ambient cabinet glow. Typography: Display face — something arcade-y and chunky. Google Fonts: "Bungee" for display (chunky, arcade signage), body: "Space Grotesk" or "IBM Plex Sans" for readability. Numbers: "Bungee" or a mono. Let's use Bungee for display/marquee, and "Space Grotesk" for body, plus maybe "JetBrains Mono" for stats readouts. Three faces is fine. Features to make it feel alive: - Canvas game with paddle, ball, blocks. - Multiple levels with generated layouts (pyramid, arch, checker, wall, tunnel). - Power-ups falling: expand paddle, multiball, slow ball, laser? (maybe keep: wide, multiball, slow, life, sticky). Laser is fun — add it. - Particle explosions on block break, block hit flash, screen shake. - Combo counter with multiplier, floating score text. - Trail on ball. - CRT scanline overlay + vignette + subtle chromatic feel. - Sound via WebAudio (blips), with mute toggle. - HUD: score, high score (localStorage), lives, level, combo. - Start overlay, level-clear transition, game over, win. - Controls: mouse move, arrow keys/A-D, click/space to launch, P pause. - Side panel with power-up legend, level progress bar. - Micro-interactions: buttons with hover, keycap hints. - Marquee title with animated flicker/neon. - Responsive: canvas scales. Layout: an asymmetric arcade cabinet layout — left rail with vertical stats, center screen, right rail with power-ups & level info. Marquee across top spanning full width with title in Bungee, big. Below, a footer strip with controls legend. Let me be careful with canvas sizing: fixed internal resolution (e.g., 800x600 or 720x560) and CSS scaling with aspect-ratio. Use devicePixelRatio for crispness. Let me write the game carefully. Game constants: - W = 880, H = 660 internal. - Paddle: w 110, h 14, y = H - 46. - Ball: r 8, speed base 6.2. - Blocks: cols 12, cell width = (W - 2*margin) / cols. Block types: normal (1 hit), tough (2 hits, armored), steel (indestructible), explosive (chain). Colors per row. Power-ups: chance ~14% from destroyed blocks. - W: widen paddle - M: multiball (split into 3) - S: slow - L: laser (paddle shoots, space/click fires) - +: extra life - C: catch (sticky) — maybe skip for complexity? Sticky is nice. Let's include but keep simple: ball sticks, press space to release. Actually let's include: W, M, S, L, +, and a shield (temporary bottom barrier)? Keep 6: W, M, S, L, +, C. Effects timed with duration. Level layouts: define patterns as functions returning block list. 8 levels then "endless" with increasing speed. Let's do 10 levels with distinct patterns, then win screen. Physics: circle-rect collision with proper axis resolution. Simple approach: for each block, check AABB vs circle; compute overlap on x and y, resolve smaller axis, flip corresponding velocity component. Good enough. Paddle collision: reflect with angle based on offset, plus speed increase slightly. Wall collisions: left/right/top. Bottom: lose ball. Screen shake: offset canvas translate. Particles: on block destroy, spawn 10-16 squares with velocity, gravity, fade. Ball trail: store last N positions, draw fading circles. Combo: consecutive block hits without touching paddle → multiplier up to x8. Resets on paddle hit. Score: base 50 * combo multiplier * level factor. Sound: WebAudio oscillator blips: paddle (square 440), wall (square 300), block (saw with pitch by row), powerup (arpeggio), lose (descending), level clear (fanfare). Mute toggle button. Now the HTML/CSS design. Structure: ```
title + tagline + high score
score, level, lives, combo meter
canvas + overlays + scanlines
power-up legend, controls, stats
controls keycaps, buttons
``` Background: layered — radial glows in teal/amber, a faint dot grid, and animated diagonal light sweep. Plus a subtle noise. Colors: - ink: #0d1b22 (deep teal-ink) - panel: #12262f - amber: #ffb347 / #f6a01f - coral: #ff5f6d - cyan: #3ddbd9 - lime: #a8e05f - cream text: #f2ece1 That's a warm/cool arcade mix — multi-hue, like a cabinet lit up. Good. Marquee: big Bungee title "BLOCK BUSTER" with layered text-shadow neon, plus a small "INSERT COIN" blinking. Add a diagonal stripe pattern band. Left rail: giant score number in Bungee with tabular feel, level indicator, lives as little ball icons, combo meter bar that fills. Right rail: power-up legend chips with colored badges, hover reveals description; run stats (blocks broken, longest combo, balls launched). Footer: keycap-styled control hints + buttons (Start/Pause, Sound, Restart). Overlays inside screen: start card, level card, game over card — animated in. Micro-interactions: buttons with translate/shadow on hover, keycaps depress, rail items slide, powerup chips glow when active with a timer ring. Also add active power-up indicators floating over the screen top-right with countdown bars. Let me write the code. Canvas rendering details: - Background inside playfield: dark gradient + faint grid + parallax dots drifting. - Blocks drawn with rounded rect, top highlight, and a "crack" overlay for damaged. - Paddle: rounded capsule with gradient and glow, plus LED segments. - Ball: white core with glow and trail. Let me handle input: mousemove over canvas → paddle target x; touch support; keyboard left/right with acceleration. Paddle movement: smooth lerp to target when mouse used; keyboard sets velocity. Pause on blur. Let me write it. Key code sections: ```js const CV = document.getElementById('game'); const ctx = CV.getContext('2d'); const W = 880, H = 660; function fitCanvas(){ dpr; CV.width = W*dpr; CV.height=H*dpr; ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0); } ``` CSS: canvas width 100%, aspect-ratio 880/660. Game state object. Level definitions: use string maps! Nice: array of strings where chars map to block types. 12 columns. Chars: '.' empty, '1' normal, '2' tough(2hp), '3' steel, 'X' explosive, 'P' pick? no. Let me define 10 maps of 12 cols x up to 10 rows. Level 1: simple rows ``` "............", "111111111111", "111111111111", "111111111111", ``` Level 2: pyramid Level 3: checker with tough Level 4: arch/tunnel with steel pillars Level 5: diamond with explosive Level 6: fortress with steel walls Level 7: zigzag Level 8: brick with tough mix + steel Level 9: space
